account_thesis: Two Ohio sites, two definitions of dwell.

touches.subject: Ohio gate roles
touches.body:
Hi Jordan,

Acme Foods posted three gate-clerk roles at the Ohio distribution center in August [[SRC:E1]]. Two of them are night shift.

My guess is the clerks exist to keep inbound trailers moving when the dock and the lot disagree about what is where.

How many trailers sit past their appointment on a normal Tuesday?

Casey Larkin, YardFlow by FreightRoll
touches.cta: How many trailers sit past their appointment on a normal Tuesday?
touches.next_step: if reply: engage directly; if silence: step 2 on day 4

touches.subject: Dayton plant
touches.body:
Hi Jordan,

Acme Foods opened a new plant in Dayton [[SRC:E2]], and the receiving side of a new plant usually inherits the gate routine of the nearest older site.

If Dayton checks drivers in on paper the way the Ohio distribution center does, the two sites will disagree about dwell before the first quarter closes.

Worth sending over the yard-network scorecard?

Casey Larkin, YardFlow by FreightRoll
touches.cta: Worth sending over the yard-network scorecard?

touches.subject: Paper at the gate
touches.body:
Hi Jordan,

Acme Foods runs paper check-in at the Ohio gate [[SRC:E4]], which is the pattern where the guard shack and the dock office keep two different lists of the same trailers.

My guess is the night clerks spend their shift reconciling those lists rather than moving freight.

Reply and I'll send the short version.

Casey Larkin, YardFlow by FreightRoll
touches.cta: Reply and I'll send the short version.

touches.subject: Sequencing the Ohio program
touches.body:
Hi Jordan,

Acme Foods announced an automation program for its Ohio yards [[SRC:E3]], and automation lands badly when the gate still runs on a clipboard.

The order of operations that held at Primo Brands is at https://yardflow.ai/order-of-operations/ if the sequencing question is live at Acme.

Worth sending over the yard-network scorecard?

Casey Larkin, YardFlow by FreightRoll

touches.subject: Dock doors and dwell
touches.body:
Hi Riley,

The 110 dock doors at the Ohio distribution center likely receive from two yards that keep separate check-in sheets, so the same trailer can be waiting on one list and moving on the other.

My guess is the dispatch desk spends the first hour of every shift reconciling those two sheets.

Worth sending over the yard-network scorecard?

touches.subject: Half the turn is waiting
touches.body:
Hi Riley,

Acme Foods posted three gate-clerk roles at the Ohio distribution center in August [[SRC:E1]], and a clerk hire usually means the check-in line is being managed by hand.

My guess is the same split holds in Ohio: at Primo, half of the turn was pure wait, not the physical move, measured in a side-by-side pilot.

Reply and I'll send the short version.

Casey Larkin, YardFlow by FreightRoll

touches.subject: Ohio Gate Comparison Note
touches.body:
Hi Riley,

My guess is the two Ohio yards will keep disagreeing about dwell until one check-in routine runs at both, and pricing is the usual reason that conversation stalls.

The proof page at https://yardflow.ai/proof/ shows what one common routine looked like at Primo Brands.

Worth sending over the yard-network scorecard?
